channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: FULL LIST: Meet the African billionaires who own luxury brands around the world
item.description: Africa’s roster of billionaires is a fascinating mix of industrial titans, financiers, and cultural influencers. Yet only a handful have direct or meaningful connections to luxury brands, whether through ownership, significant stakes, or founding luxury ventures.

item.title: Morocco to open $5.6 billion port hosting its first liquefied natural gas terminal
item.description: Morocco is set to bring its second Mediterranean deepwater port, Nador West Med, into operation in the fourth quarter of this year.

item.title: Cairo and Johannesburg ranked among the most powerful cities in the world
item.description: Africa made a modest but notable appearance in this year’s ranking of the world’s most powerful cities.

item.title: AES faces first major economic test after ECOWAS exit as currency rumours hit setback
item.description: Speculation that the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) might fast-track a single currency to signal regional unity hit a setback after Mali’s Ministry of Economy and Finance denied any roadmap or timeline, raising questions about how the bloc will coordinate economically outside ECOWAS.

item.title: U.S. escalates sanctions threat on Rwanda as eastern Congo peace deal faces setback
item.description: Washington is escalating pressure on Rwanda as the U.S.-brokered peace deal aimed at stabilising eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) struggles to take hold, triggering growing frustration within President Donald Trump’s administration and the U.S. Congress.

item.title: The UAE is transferring fighter jets to African nations, but France decides who benefits
item.description: The United Arab Emirates is retiring its Dassault Mirage 2000‑9 fighter jets as it prepares to take delivery of new Rafale F4 multirole fighters from France, part of one of the largest Rafale export orders globally.

item.title: Nigeria touts a $2.5 billion plan to end its electricity problems
item.description: The persistent and detrimental issue of Nigeria's power sector is currently being addressed with a significant government intervention aimed at resolving the perennial blackouts that plague the nation.

item.title: From structural adjustments to resource takeover, inside Mali’s bold fight for its gold
item.description: Mali's Gold has traditionally been considered more than just a resource. Today, it serves as a strategic asset and geopolitical tool, influencing national policy, international investment, and political decision-making.

item.title: DR Congo set to export 100,000 tons of copper from Chinese-run mines to the United States
item.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo has confirmed plans to ship 100,000 metric tons of copper from a Chinese-run mine to the United States by the end of January, following its submission to the U.S. administration of a list of state-backed mining projects for potential investment

item.title: Canal+ forecasts $479 million in annual synergies by 2030 after $3 billion MultiChoice acquisition
item.description: French media group Canal+ has outlined significant cost-saving expectations from its $3 billion acquisition of South African pay-TV operator MultiChoice, sending its shares to record highs on Thursday, January 29, 2026.
